whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no `reviews[]` entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no `reviews[]` entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author, and I am the author of every path above. Reviewer designation for a Coder compliance-path commit is the CTO (MediaTech). There is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost), so a CTO review is a recorded degradation, not independent review -- stated here rather than implied. The commit this claim covers WILL report an R2 violation until the CTO records a verdict, and that violation is the honest state. Writing a `reviews[]` entry naming myself would turn a control into a rubber stamp. This migration touches consent history (personal data) and the Directus grant ceiling, so per the Coder instructions it goes to the CTO regardless.

It is not clearance of the retention gate (plan 0.10.5), which only the CEO can clear. Non-compliance-path files changed on the same issue (delivery-log routes, shared collections/role-matrix/types, web contract test) are ordinary code, committed separately without this claim, not claimed here.
